phase.title: MCP integration and mock tool server
phase.goal: Connect the agent's tool boundary to MCP and demonstrate controlled execution against a separate mock factory-data server.

why_this_phase_exists: Prove that external tools can change independently behind ToolExecutor while the Agent Loop continues to consume only provider-neutral ToolCall and ToolResult contracts.
implementation_guidelines: Follow docs/requirements/project-brief.md: Keep implementation clean and Retry and cancellation ownership by phase.
Reuse MCP SDK protocol support and existing core results/events; use suitable SDK retry support or a small explicit adapter loop, not a generic retry framework.
in_scope: Implement ToolExecutor with an MCP client adapter; the Agent Loop continues to see only ToolCall and ToolResult.
Create a separate mock MCP server with two or three deterministic factory-oriented tools.
Discover tool names and argument schemas from the MCP server, intersect them with the runtime-approved set, and expose only that intersection to the model.

Open one application-scoped async MCP session before runs, discover once per connection and retain SDK schema caches; explicit refresh/reconnect invalidates executor catalogs. Never cache live results.
Enforce an approved-tool allowlist before dispatch.
Validate tool arguments against the declared schema before dispatch.
Add per-call timeouts and explicitly bounded retry behavior.
Use async provider-neutral I/O ports, loop and harness, sharing bounded cancellation/deadline mechanics without leaking SDK types into core.
Normalize MCP successes and failures into core ToolResult and RuntimeError contracts without leaking MCP SDK objects.
Handle unknown tools, remote tool errors, slow responses, connection loss, and malformed responses.
Bound in-flight requests; isolate per-run cancellation and serialize connection establishment. Add in-memory same-session run exclusion and late-output checks.
out_of_scope: A dynamic plugin ecosystem or arbitrary shell, filesystem, and network tools
Automatic retry of side-effecting tools after an ambiguous connection failure
boundaries_introduced: MCP is an infrastructure adapter behind ToolExecutor and is invisible to AgentLoop.
The independently runnable mock MCP server owns all factory-specific concepts.
Tool discovery describes server capability; the runtime allowlist independently grants agent execution authority.
contracts_introduced: Tools exposed to the model equal tools discovered from MCP intersected with tools approved by the runtime.
MCP responses are normalized into the Phase 1 ToolResult contract.
Every remote attempt retains the originating tool_call_id for traceability.
A connection loss after dispatch may represent uncertain external side effects and is not treated as proof that the tool did not execute.

mock_tools.name: get_machine_status
mock_tools.purpose: Return deterministic status and readings for a machine identifier.

mock_tools.name: list_open_work_orders
mock_tools.purpose: Return deterministic open work orders for an area or line.

mock_tools.name: get_safety_procedure
mock_tools.purpose: Return a short deterministic procedure for an approved procedure code.

failure_policy.unknown_tool: Reject locally without contacting the MCP server and return a non-retryable structured error to the loop.
failure_policy.unapproved_tool: Reject locally even when the MCP server advertises the tool; do not expose or dispatch it.
failure_policy.invalid_arguments: Reject locally with validation details and return a non-retryable structured error to the loop.
failure_policy.tool_error: Return a structured tool error to the loop. Retry only when the adapter recognizes a transient failure and the tool is safe to repeat; do not retry a logical tool failure.
failure_policy.timeout: Cancel or abandon the in-flight call at the configured deadline and return a timeout result.
failure_policy.connection_loss: Return a transport error. Retry only when the tool is read-only or explicitly safe to repeat, cancellation is absent, and both attempt and deadline budgets remain.
failure_policy.malformed_response: Reject malformed MCP output at the adapter and return a structured non-SDK error.
failure_policy.ambiguous_side_effect: Do not automatically retry a side-effecting tool when the connection fails after dispatch because execution may already have occurred.
failure_policy.retry_rule: Retry only a known transient failure for a safe-to-repeat tool. Unknown errors default to non-retryable. Never exceed max_attempts or the remaining run deadline.

retry_and_timeout_policy.owner: MCPToolExecutor owns tool retries. SDKMCPClient reconnects/discovers but never retries a tool. SDK input-required replay is disabled.
retry_and_timeout_policy.eligibility: All conditions must hold: the failure is explicitly classified as transient, the tool is read-only or explicitly safe to repeat, no cancellation is pending, and both attempt and deadline budgets remain. RuntimeError.retryable is a hint, not sufficient authorization by itself.
retryable_cases: Tool timeout when the operation is safe to repeat.
Temporary MCP unavailability or connection reset identified by known exception types or MCP error codes for a safe-to-repeat tool.
non_retryable_cases: Invalid arguments or schema validation failure.
Malformed MCP response or unknown internal exception.
A deterministic tool or business error that the same input will reproduce.
An ambiguous side-effecting call that may already have executed.
retry_and_timeout_policy.budget: Use max_attempts=2 for the assessment mock tools, including the initial request, so at most one retry occurs. max_attempts=1 disables retry. Each attempt uses the smaller of the per-call timeout and remaining run time; retry never resets the run deadline.
retry_and_timeout_policy.wait: Use one short fixed configurable delay, default 200 milliseconds for the local demo. Tests set the delay to zero. Exponential backoff and jitter remain future production refinements.
retry_and_timeout_policy.cancellation: Check cancellation before discovery/attempts and during all waits. Per-request cancellation preserves the shared session. Connection closure wakes pending I/O. SDK process cleanup may exceed the request deadline. Core rejects late output now; Phase 3 persists lifecycle and diagnostic records. No remote rollback guarantee.
retry_and_timeout_policy.trace: Reuse tool_execution_started, tool_execution_failed, and tool_execution_completed with attempt, max_attempts, tool_call_id, retry_reason, and retry_delay_ms in their payload where applicable. If the adapter needs execution context, extend the provider-neutral port with the smallest callback/context needed. Do not add a retry event hierarchy. Return one final ToolResult per logical call.
retry_and_timeout_policy.usage: Adapter attempts do not increment logical Usage.tool_calls; events expose attempts and all attempts/waits consume the deadline. A model-requested repeat is a new logical call.
retry_and_timeout_policy.ambiguous_effects: Track outcome_unknown independently of retryable, including cancellation and malformed responses after possible dispatch. Block identical unsafe calls in the same executor until the outcome is resolved; known pre-dispatch failure does not poison the guard. Demo tools remain read-only; a side-effect fixture proves a new model call ID cannot bypass the exact name/arguments guard. Durable reconciliation and business-level equivalence remain outside Phase 2.
retry_and_timeout_policy.exhaustion: Return a structured ToolResult failure after transient attempts are exhausted. Cancellation or run-deadline exhaustion prevents further scheduling.

deliverables: Separate mock MCP server with two or three tools
Timeout, retry, and error normalization policies
Integration tests using controlled MCP fixtures

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The deterministic agent loop completes a multi-step task using a result returned by the mock MCP server.
An unknown or unapproved tool is rejected without remote execution and is visible in run events.
Invalid arguments never reach the mock tool implementation.
Tool error, timeout, and connection-loss cases terminate or continue according to documented policy without hanging the run.
The mock MCP server can be started independently from the agent runtime.
Only the intersection of discovered and approved tools is advertised to the model, and MCP SDK types never appear in the Agent Loop.
An ambiguous connection failure does not automatically retry a side-effecting tool.
Async application-scoped MCP lifecycle reuses a ready connection, isolates request cancellation and revalidates after bounded reconnect; close cleans up owned resources.

required_tests: Successful MCP tool discovery and execution
Actual connection and tools/list counts: one discovery pass per connection, several fresh calls, explicit refresh and reconnect invalidate the catalog
Discovery consumes remaining run time and cancellation before discovery prevents server contact
Unknown or disallowed tool
Discovered but unapproved tool is not advertised or dispatched
Invalid tool arguments
Remote tool returns an error
MCP response exceeds timeout
MCP connection drops
Malformed MCP response is normalized
Ambiguous failure of a side-effecting tool is not automatically retried
Transient retry stays within its configured budget
Transient failure then success returns one ToolResult and ordered attempt events; max_attempts=1 disables retries
Permanent or unknown errors do not retry and SDK retries cannot multiply the documented budget
Cancel during a retry wait or exhaust the run deadline: no further attempt starts
Actual stdio timeout and cancellation honor request time plus bounded SDK cleanup grace, with watchdog and owned-process exit checks
A model-requested repeat cannot bypass the ambiguous-side-effect guard
A deterministic tool or business error is returned to the model without an automatic retry
Tool attempt and result events contain correlation identifiers
Agent Loop test remains free of MCP SDK imports
Cancel one of two in-flight requests without closing the shared session or cancelling the other
Capacity wait timeout is pre-dispatch and leaves connection healthy
Concurrent reconnect callers share one startup; short/cancelled waiters do not cancel that startup
Changed or removed schema/retry safety after reconnect prevents unsafe dispatch
Startup failure and idempotent shutdown leave no owned process or lifecycle task; pending calls observe closure
Async provider cancel/deadline rejects late completion and the harness rejects overlapping runs on one session
deferred_decisions: Concrete RPC transport and event delivery
Production authentication and MCP service discovery
HTTP Retry-After, HTTP reconnect behavior and transport-specific retry accounting; Phase 2 validates local stdio and in-process MCP only
Policies for a larger or dynamically changing tool catalog
Automatic catalog-change subscriptions, cross-process connection ownership and production load testing
exit_condition: The core can execute only approved, validated MCP tools and all required MCP failure modes are bounded, normalized, and traceable.

session_lifecycle.ownership: Application owns one client per server/configuration/security context on one asyncio event loop. A dedicated task enters/exits the SDK context. No pool or sync-wrapper thread.
session_lifecycle.startup: async with SDKMCPClient connects and discovers with startup_timeout_seconds (default 5), then executor discovery applies allowlisting before admission. Failure keeps the client not ready.
session_lifecycle.catalog: One paginated discovery pass per connection; SDK output-schema cache is reused. Explicit refresh increments catalog_version. Tool responses remain fresh.
session_lifecycle.reconnect: One connection lock coalesces waiting callers; each reconnect makes one bounded connection attempt. A cancelled/short waiter does not cancel shared startup. Reconnect reloads schema and retry safety; expected_catalog_version blocks stale dispatch. No automatic tool replay.
session_lifecycle.capacity: Default max_in_flight=8 per client; capacity, lock and reconnect waits consume each request's budget. No cross-process coordination.
session_lifecycle.cancellation: Cancel only the request, preserving healthy shared I/O. Connection closure interrupts pending calls. Core rechecks cancellation/deadline before accepting output; remote rollback is not guaranteed.
session_lifecycle.shutdown: Application stops admission and finishes/cancels runs before closing the client. aclose is idempotent, aborts pending I/O and awaits SDK cleanup in the owner task. RPC admission/drain wiring belongs to Phase 4.
session_lifecycle.limitations: Asyncio only; tested stdio and in-process transports. No automatic list-changed subscription, HTTP validation, durable session guard or durable outcome reconciliation yet.
